learning_objective: 🎯 Explore how independent India rebuilt its economy through Five Year Plans, the Green Revolution, and protectionist industrial policies.

key_vocabulary.definition: A centralized economic program outlining the government's investment and development targets over five years.
The massive increase in agricultural production due to the use of High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation.
Changes in land ownership laws, including the abolition of intermediaries and setting a ceiling on maximum land holdings.
An inward-looking trade policy aiming to replace imported goods with domestically produced ones to save foreign exchange.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: India adopted a mixed economy. The Planning Commission (established in 1950) drove development through four main goals: 1) Growth (increasing GDP), 2) Modernisation (adopting new technology), 3) Self-reliance (reducing dependence on foreign goods), and 4) Equity (ensuring benefits reach the poor).

To solve food shortages, India introduced Land Reforms (abolishing Zamindars, land ceilings) and the Green Revolution (1960s). HYV seeds of wheat and rice dramatically increased yields, making India self-sufficient in food grains, though it initially benefited only rich farmers in regions like Punjab.

The government took the leading role in industrialization. Industries were classified into three schedules (State-owned, Mixed, and Private). The private sector was strictly regulated through a 'License Raj' system. Small-Scale Industries (SSIs) were protected to promote employment.

India followed an 'inward-looking trade strategy' called Import Substitution. The government protected domestic industries from foreign competition by imposing high tariffs (taxes on imports) and quotas (limits on import quantities).

fun_activity.title: 📜 The License Raj Maze
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you want to start a shoe factory in 1980. You can't just buy machines and start! You have to get a license from the government to open it. If you want to make 500 shoes instead of 200, you need another license! If you want to introduce a new design, another license! This strict control was called the 'License Raj'.

exam_tips: 📌 'Growth with Equity' is a frequent question. Explain that economic growth (higher GDP) means nothing if the wealth is concentrated among a few rich people; equity ensures the poor also benefit.
📌 The Green Revolution had two phases. Phase 1 (1960s-70s) was restricted to wheat and rich states (Punjab, Haryana). Phase 2 (1970s-80s) spread to more crops and states.
📌 The Karve Committee (1955) highlighted the importance of Small Scale Industries (SSIs) for generating employment in rural areas.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Mahalanobis model formed the basis of the Second Five Year Plan, focusing heavily on rapid industrialization and heavy industries.
⭐ Land ceilings were often evaded by big landlords who registered extra land under the names of their relatives.
⭐ Subsidies on fertilizers encouraged the adoption of HYV seeds but later became a massive financial burden on the government.
